subject: Transport Layer Recommendation: TLS Tunnel vs Endpoint Attachment for Kestrel Systems Private Deploy
messages:
From: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Perez <alex.perez@kestrelsys.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, connor_obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 04 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Transport Layer Recommendation: TLS Tunnel vs Endpoint Attachment for Kestrel Systems Private Deploy

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, Kestrel's primary goals are: low-latency inference for the driver-routing service (95th pct target < 80ms), strict egress control for PCI-adjacent telemetry, and a minimal ops footprint for the initial pilot. We ran Redwood's access matrix against your constraints and sketched two viable transports: (A) TLS tunnel (mutual-TLS) over a dedicated public egress with source-NAT, and (B) interface endpoint (PrivateLink-style) with customer-managed VPC endpoint service.

Attached is a short connectivity matrix (kestrel_connectivity_matrix.xlsx) that summarizes tradeoffs across latency, ops, compliance, and failover. High-level recommendation: start pilot on the TLS tunnel with mTLS + connection-anchoring for low-latency reads, and stage a PrivateLink endpoint in parallel for the production rollout where stricter control and no public egress is required. Rationale in one line: TLS tunnel is faster to onboard and easier for your edge devices; PrivateLink reduces the exposed surface and aligns with your procurement security requirements for production.

Next steps we propose:
- Redwood to provision a test ingress (mutual-TLS) for pilot (ETA 2 weeks).
- Kestrel to run a 48-hour latency & packet-path capture against the tunnel.
- If pilot meets 95th pct latency target, move to scope PrivateLink for production (procurement/contract step).

I've attached a short playbook (redwood_tls_tunnel_playbook.pdf) and the matrix. Ben and Connor are looped for implementation and ops runbook items.

Would you like us to open a HubSpot opportunity and a DocuSign for the pilot agreement once procurement confirms?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: kestrel_connectivity_matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]
[Attachment: redwood_tls_tunnel_playbook.pdf (application/pdf)]

Cc: procurement@kestrelsys.com
Date: Fri, 04 Jun 2027 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Transport Layer Recommendation: TLS Tunnel vs Endpoint Attachment for Kestrel Systems Private Deploy

Kimberly —

Appreciate the clear breakdown and the attachments. Quick clarifications from our side: our edge devices will be distributed across 3 cloud regions and some telco POPs; source-NAT is acceptable during pilot but we need deterministic source IPs for PCI routing in production. A couple items: 

• Can you quantify expected extra latency the TLS tunnel adds vs PrivateLink for a 512-token inference call?
• For PrivateLink, what are the operational duties expected of Kestrel (VPC endpoint creation, NACL updates, route table updates)?

Procurement will confirm the pilot SOW if we can see a simple contract stub. Please include an implementation timeline in the contract.

—Alex
Alex Perez
Head of Platform Engineering
Kestrel Systems

Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Transport Layer Recommendation: TLS Tunnel vs Endpoint Attachment for Kestrel Systems Private Deploy

Alex —

Quick answers to your questions:

• Latency: in our lab for a 512-token model (gpt-small-ish test bed) we saw median delta ~6–12ms extra round-trip for a well-provisioned mTLS tunnel vs a PrivateLink-style interface endpoint in the same region. 95th pct delta widened to ~18–30ms under bursty loads. The numbers are sensitive to TCP/TLS handshake placement and whether the edge keeps persistent connections; our playbook recommends connection anchoring + keepalive to mitigate handshake cost.

• Operational duties for PrivateLink: Kestrel will need to create the interface endpoint in your VPC(s), accept a service connection if you use cross-account endpoints, update route tables/NACLs as appropriate, and maintain the ENI lifecycle. Redwood will publish the endpoint-service name and provide security group recommendations; we can script the provisioning (CloudFormation/Terraform) as part of the pilot SOW.

I'll attach a short perf excerpt and the terraform snippets in the pilot repo once we greenlight.

—Ben Carter
Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

2) Kestrel (Alex) confirm preferred CIDR block(s) for the pilot egress anchors and whether you'll accept source-NAT during the pilot.
3) Procurement (procurement@kestrelsys.com) will advise if a security questionnaire is required prior to DocuSign.

I'll follow up with the SOW draft and the Terraform repo link. Looking forward to getting the pilot on the road.

Regards,

Redwood Inference
